      <description>Klimaminister Sigrun Aasland (Ap) har med en stor sum når hun mandag reiser til åpningen av klimatoppmøtet i Tyrkia.
– Vi har med 600 millioner kroner til Brasil, for de har levert veldig gode resultater på å hindre avskoging i 2025, sier Aasland.

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/kongen-fullforte-maraton-pa-tiden-4.43.01-1.18076803</link>
      <description>Kongen og kronprinsessen er deltakere i French Riviera Marathon, i Nice sør i Frankrike.
Kong Haakon løp i mål på tiden 4.43.01, ifølge sporingstjenesten Trackanza.
Det var TV 2 som meldte saken først.
Et bilde viser kongen og kronprinsessen løpende ved siden av hverandre under maratonet. I maratonet er kronprinsessen registrert som Ingrid Alexandra og kongen som Haakon Magnus.
Startskuddet gikk klokka 09.16, og distansen er helmaraton på 42,125 kilometer. Løypen går langs den franske rivieraen fra Nice til Cannes.
Lørdag formiddag opplyste Slottet på nettsidene sine at «statsrådet forestår bestyrelsen av riket».
Ifølge nettsidene var kongen og kronprinsessen på privat opphold i utlandet. Det betyr at regjeringen har ansvaret for å styre og forvalte landet.
(NTB/NRK)</description>

    <item>
      <title>Ny norsk gulltriumf i VM i skyting</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/ny-norsk-gulltriumf-i-vm-i-skyting-1.18076796</link>
      <description>Caroline Finnestad Lund, Jeanette Hegg Duestad og Synnøve Berg tok laggullet på 50 meter rifle match i VM i skyting i Doha søndag.
Det var Lunds andre gull i mesterskapet. Lørdag ble 21-åringen verdensmester på 50 meter 60 skudd liggende.
Norge sanket totalt 1764 poeng under lagkonkurransen, og de kom 3,0 poeng foran Sveits på 2.-plass. Tsjekkia stakk av med bronsemedaljen. De var to poeng bak sveitserne igjen.
I eliminasjonen for lag 1 ble Finnestad Lund nummer fire med 588 poeng. Synnøve Berg ble nummer sju med 586 poeng. Duestad ble nummer tre med 590 poeng i lag 2.
Alle de tre norske jentene er videre til kvalifiseringen i den individuelle konkurransen i den samme øvelsen mandag. (NTB)</description>

      <title>Flere skadet etter kraftig jordskjelv sentralt i Japan</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/flere-skadet-etter-kraftig-jordskjelv-sentralt-i-japan-1.18076688</link>
      <description>Minst 22 personer ble skadet da et jordskjelv med styrke 5,5 rammet Shizuoka-prefekturet i det sentrale Japan. Butikkvinduer ble knust, og folk rømte ut av bygninger.
Ifølge kringkasteren NHK er det ikke fare for tsunamier.
Skjelvet inntraff rundt klokka 1 natt til søndag. Det hadde en dybde på 41 kilometer. Den foreløpige målingen fra Japans meteorologiske institutt, som har ansvaret for overvåking og varsling av jordskjelv, var på 5,7.
Det amerikanske jordskjelvsenteret USGS målte det til 5,5.
I naboprefekturet Aichi ble det målt kraftige rystelser på nivå 5+ på den japanske skalaen – det sterkeste som er registrert der siden 1997.
(NTB)</description>

      <description>Israels president har gitt opposisjonsleder Gadi Eisenkot i oppdrag å prøve danne regjering.
Hverken partiene som støtter statsminister Benjamin Netanyahu eller partiene som støtter Eisenkot fikk flertall ved valget 27. november.
Netanyahus blokk fikk 53 plasser i Knesset, mens blokken til Eisenkot fikk 48 mandater.
For å få flertall og bli statsminister trenger man 61 plasser i nasjonalforsamlingen. Begge blokkene er avhengig av de 19 mandatene fra de palestinsk-arabiske partiene, mend både Netanyahu og Eisenkot har sagt de ikke vil forhandle med dem.</description>

      <description>Casper Ruud har storspilt i Paris denne uken. Nå er han klar for semifinale etter seier over Nuno Borges.
Ruuds oppgjør mot portugiseren endte med 7-6 (7-5), 6-4. De to møttes for bare ni dager siden i Basel, og da snudde Borges kampen til seier.
Ruud og Borges kom til semifinalen proppfulle av selvtillit: Ingen har tapt ett sett på veien, og de hadde heller ikke gitt fra seg mer enn fire game i noen av settene.

      <description>Politiet opplyser at det har vært en front-mot-front-ulykke på E6 like ved Eidsvoll-tunnelen i sørgående løp.
Ulykken skjedde ved kryss nummer 56 Boksrud. En av bilene kjørte nordover i det sørgående løpet, ifølge politiet.
Det satt en person i hver av bilene. En av dem er bekreftet død, den andre er kritisk skadet.

E6 har midlertidig omkjøring i sørgående retning. Omgjøringen går fra kryss nummer 56 Boksrud via FV1551 Trondheimsveien, og deretter ut på E6 sydgående ved Nebbenes, opplyser politiet.</description>

Familien sier til VG at Bjørn Terje Axelsen (47) døde etter noen få ukers alvorlig sykdom.
Søsteren takker personalet på Tangerudbakken borettslag.

      <description>Thomas Markle ble pågrepet av føderale agenter i nærheten av Tampa i Florida fredag morgen amerikansk tid.

    <item>
      <title>NFF innfører semiautomatisert offside i Eliteserien</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/nff-innforer-semiautomatisert-offside-i-eliteserien-1.18075445</link>
      <description>Det opplyser Fotballforbundet på en pressekonferanse fredag.
– Prisen har kommet ned til et nivå som gjør at muligheten er der, sier generalsekretær Karl-Petter Løken.
Han opplyser at innføringen vil skje i tråd med et dommerløft. NFF bevilger 5,5 millioner kroner i 2027 til dommerløftet, og 3,5 millioner av dem skal få til semiautomatisert offside.
NFF ønsker å øke dette til 7,5 millioner kroner i 2028, og gradvis trappe opp mot 2030.
– Det du har sett med disse linjene blir borte og du får disse visningene med menneskekropper hvor du ser helt tydelig at det er offside. Det er semiautomatisert offside. Det er det ene løftet, sier Løken og fortsetter:
– Det er en utgift som tas én gang og som vil følge oss, og så vil vi trappe opp resten av investeringen i dommerutviklingene i de andre tiltakene i tillegg. Så det blir en gradvis opptrapping, eksempelvis profesjonalisering. Vi starter stille og rolig og så blir det flere og flere.
Dette skjer etter et VAR-oppgjør blant flere toppklubber. Roenborg satt ned et eget utvalg som konkluderte med at «Dagens VAR fungerer for dårlig under norske forhold. De lovte forbedringene har ikke løst hovedutfordringene, og kostnadene er for høye i forhold til kvaliteten».
Utvalget til Rosenborg stilte seg også tvilende til at semiautomatisert offside ville hjelpe VAR i norsk fotball.
– Så det vil være penger ut av vinduet hvis tinget sier nei (til VAR)? spør NRK.
– Vi kommer ikke til å diskutere detaljer i den avtalen, svarer Klaveness.</description>

      <description>Den svenske regjeringen har besluttet å gjeninnføre indre grensekontroll i en periode på seks måneder.
Begrunnelsen er alvorlige trusler mot den allmenne orden og indre sikkerhet, opplyser den svenske regjeringen i en pressemelding.
Videre skriver regjeringen at vurderingen er basert på den alvorlige sikkerhetssituasjonen som følge av Russlands fullskala invasjon av Ukraina.

The warning system is designed to alert people to sudden increases in river flows, which can occur with little warning as part of hydroelectric operations.

When the sirens sound during normal operations, people are advised to immediately move out of the river channel. BC Hydro says the testing is necessary to ensure the warning system at the John Hart facility is working properly.

]]> 1360136 UVic study finds world already experiencing warming equivalent to 1.5 C climate threshold https://cheknews.ca/uvic-study-finds-world-already-experiencing-warming-equivalent-to-1-5-c-climate-threshold-1360121/ Mon, 09 Nov 2026 17:18:12 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1360121

New research from the University of Victoria suggests the world is already experiencing warming levels equivalent to those associated with the Paris Agreement’s 1.5 C climate target.

The post UVic study finds world already experiencing warming equivalent to 1.5 C climate threshold appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

New research from the University of Victoria suggests the world is already experiencing warming levels equivalent to those associated with the Paris Agreement’s 1.5 C climate target.

The study, published in Nature Climate Change, found that by the end of 2025, all regions of the world had already experienced 90 to 94 per cent of the warming expected in a world that is 1.5 C warmer than pre-industrial levels.

Researchers with UVic’s Pacific Climate Impacts Consortium (PCIC) say the findings highlight the urgency of adapting to climate change.

“Many of the climate risks associated with 1.5 C of warming are no longer a future concern; they are already being experienced around the world,” said Francis Zwiers, a statistician and scientist emeritus at PCIC, in a release.

The Paris Agreement, adopted by nearly 200 countries in 2015, aims to limit global warming to 1.5 C above pre-industrial levels to avoid the most severe impacts of climate change.

However, researchers say warming is not occurring evenly around the world.

The study found that global land temperatures have already risen an average of 1.9 C above pre-industrial levels, while northwestern North America has experienced warming of approximately 3 C.

“What is less well understood is that 1.5 C of global warming does not translate to the same amount of warming everywhere,” noted Xuebin Zhang, climate scientist and director of PCIC.

“Communities in many parts of the world are already facing much higher levels of warming and associated impacts.”

Land areas are warming faster than oceans, particularly in northern regions. Arctic areas of Russia and North America have experienced more rapid temperature increases than ocean-influenced regions such as southern South America, Southeast Asia and New Zealand.

Despite those differences, researchers estimate that all regions identified by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change will reach warming levels equivalent to those expected in a 1.5 C warmer world around 2029.

The findings come as world leaders and researchers prepare to gather for the United Nations climate change conference in Antalya, Türkiye, beginning Monday.

Researchers say the study could help governments and communities better prepare for climate change, particularly when planning infrastructure such as buildings and bridges.

“People have asked: ‘What should we be designing for in the future? What climate should we be considering?’” said Zwiers.

“Regional warming has already reached levels effectively equivalent to those of a 1.5 C world. The science underscores the urgency of adaptation everywhere, now.”

The B.C. Conservatives have gained another seat after the final count of votes in the October provincial election.

Conservative candidate David Xie reeled in NDP incumbent Paul Choi in Burnaby South-Metrotown, overcoming Choi’s 66-vote lead heading into the final count to win by 64 votes.

The final count across for the 93 ridings in the province included about 150,000 mail-in, phone and absentee ballots, while the narrowness of Choi’s previous lead also required a recount in Burnaby South-Metrotown.

The final tally extends the Conservatives’ majority, giving them 64 seats, the NDP 27 and the Greens two.

Conservative candidates took 47.4 per cent of the popular vote compared with the NDP’s 37.6 per cent and the Greens’ 11.2 per cent.

The only other riding where a recount was required because the margin was fewer than 100 votes before the final tally was Ladysmith-Oceanside, where NDP incumbent Stephanie Higginson prevailed by 50 votes after the recount and final tally.

Winds reached as high as 116 kilometres an hour on Herbert Island off northern Vancouver Island, with Victoria’s airport reaching 96 kilometres an hour and 70 kilometres an hour in places such as Prince George, Bella Bella, Tofino and Hope.

In Surrey, B.C., a driver died Saturday after two vehicles became trapped under a fallen tree.

Environment Canada issued wind warnings and special statements predicting heavy rain across large swaths of the province over the next few days.

A special weather statement covering most of B.C.’s coast and Vancouver Island says a strong and potent series of storms will approach the B.C. coast from Tuesday through Thursday, bringing heavy rain, particularly in upslope terrain and higher elevations. 

It says the rain event follows several low-pressure systems that have already drenched the region in recent days, triggering an evacuation order for about 30 properties in the village of Zeballos on the northwest coast of Vancouver Island. 

Environment Canada says there remains uncertainty about the exact amount of rain that’s coming and which regions will be affected the most, but some areas are expected to see gusty southerly winds.

]]>

Strength training and fitness are important parts of maintaining quality of life as you age, particularly for seniors over the age of 50, research shows.

Known for its coastal views, arts and cultural events, and walkable neighbourhoods, Victoria has become a sought-after living location—especially amongst the 50+ population. The 2021 Statistics Canada census data claims that more than 23% of Greater Victoria’s residents are in the retirement age group (higher than the Canadian average).

According to Keelan Clemens, the owner of local gym BPM Fitness Centre, this demographic data is increasingly reflected in his clientele. 

“Right now, I would say nearly 60% of our clients are over 50 years old,” he said. 

Clemens has been in the fitness industry for 20 years and has noticed that with the increasing retirement population, the conversations around healthy aging have also changed for the better. While aging is inevitable, losing independence and mobility doesn’t have to be. 

“The narrative has shifted from ‘any movement is good’ to ‘let’s be intentional with our movement.’ Because it’s becoming more and more apparent through research and practice that strength training for seniors is the key to maintaining quality of life.”

As we age, research is underscoring the importance of continued resistance training and functional movement. These are said to play a critical role in preserving quality of life as aging bodies naturally begin to lose muscle mass and strength if exercise becomes less of a regular habit. This process is called sarcopenia, and it impacts balance, bone health, and everyday activities like climbing stairs or lifting groceries. 

Even if you’re walking, stretching, or engaging in other low-intensity activity—which also remains important—strength training can help counter many age-related changes and reduce fall risk. 

Healthcare professionals and fitness experts know that exercise after 50 doesn’t mean pushing harder and bringing your body to the limit; instead, it’s about training smarter and incorporating a strength- and balance-focused program created by a hired professional. 

Personal Trainers who specialize in movement, mobility, and effective exercise are in high demand and can be found at gyms like BPM Fitness Centre. Their programs are specifically tailored to each individual and go beyond the generic, focusing on maintaining range of motion and building strength for your everyday life. 

Those over 50 looking to regain and maintain muscle and independence can find experienced trainers at BPM Fitness Centre. With a combined experience in kinesiology, biomechanics, and exercise science, their wealth of knowledge creates programs dedicated to improvement and support, every step of the way.

Move better to live better.

Growing older doesn’t mean slowing down. 

Visit the BPM website here to learn more about personal training for seniors in Victoria.

Sources: Statistics Canada Census (2021), Public Health Agency of Canada, BC Injury Research and Prevention Unit, NIH strength training and healthy aging research, International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health

]]>

British Columbia’s human rights tribunal has ruled that a private laboratory provider must pay $32,000 in damages, along with other costs, for discriminating against transgender and non-binary patients.

The tribunal found LifeLabs and its subsidiary Excelleris Technologies misgendered and outed three patients at clinics in Vancouver and Burnaby in 2019.

Its decision says a non-binary person was told they had to choose either male or female to receive lab services and was outed to other patients by being required to discuss their gender identity in a public space.

It also says one transgender patient was unable to update their gender marker on medical records, and another was misgendered on lab reports and opted out of necessary cancer screening to avoid being misgendered again.

The tribunal heard last year from one expert who said gender-diverse people face barriers in accessing health care, and that misgendering can be a “significant source of distress.”

Tribunal member Theressa Etmanski says LifeLabs must update its policies and staff training around gender identity, and make available to transgender and non-binary patients private spaces to discuss their identity.

“Information about a patient’s sex may be medically relevant in the provision of laboratory services. However, I wish to be clear that there is no evidence before me to support that the standard is medically necessary or justified,” Etmanski says in the decision issued Oct. 29, 2026. 

This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 8, 2026

In propulsion system design, engineers have long faced a trade-off between solid and liquid rocket fuels.
